title: Trim the extension tests without weakening them

version_files.format: ` * [VERSION] x.y.z` comment line, carried into js/round_dynamic.js by the build

repo_conventions.test_command: node chrome-extension/tests.js && node js/tests.js && node js/doc-tests.js && node claude-code-plugin/tests.js && node scripts/build-sheets.js --check
repo_conventions.branch_naming: <type>/<label>, type one of feature, fix, refactor, docs, chore, plan; each sprint names its branch

sprints.label: planted-bug-script
sprints.goal: The runner records every assertion, and one script measures, sorts, and proves as the plan's section 3 states.
sprints.scope: Runner and `eq`: the record mode in section 3.1; the sidebar piece's direct count changes (sidebar-tests.js:523-547) become `eq` calls. `scripts/planted-bugs.js`: the lexer, the planted bug table, worker copies, the four outcomes, the three modes (measure, sort, prove), the caps in the Simplicity section. `scripts/planted-bugs-test.js`: runs the script on a synthetic product file and a synthetic suite of a few assertions, with a known answer for every mode; it runs in seconds and joins the test command. Docs (`docs:` commit): the four terms in the plan's Context section go into docs/vocabulary.md, "Working terms"; CONTRIBUTING.md gains how to run the three modes.
sprints.out_of_scope: The Sheets, plugin, and Python suites; any change to a test piece beyond the sidebar count changes.
acceptance_criteria: On the synthetic fixture, `measure` gives the known catch lists, `sort` gives the known three lists, and `prove` fails on a branch that deletes a unique assertion and passes on one that deletes a repeating assertion.
A planted bug that loops forever stops at the time cap and counts as caught by a timeout.
`prove` fails with "measure again" on a branch that changes product code.
The extension suite still reports 4,623 assertions, with and without a record path.
sprints.dev_notes: Write the record at process exit, so an assertion that runs after a timer is recorded. Named constants CLEAN_RUNS = 3, TIME_CAP_MULTIPLE = 3, MAX_PLANTED_BUGS = 10000, in the script. Skip js/round_dynamic.js and claude-code-plugin/hooks/library.js; plant bugs only in chrome-extension/ outside tests/. Worker copies are git worktrees in the operating system's temporary folder, removed at the end (section 3.4). Also run `measure` on one product file to confirm real runs work end to end and report the time per planted bug.

sprints.label: case-table-rule
sprints.goal: AGENTS.md states that tests differing only by input and expected result share one case table per setup.
sprints.scope: One rule under "Code style" in AGENTS.md; "case table" in docs/vocabulary.md if planted-bug-script has not merged, else no vocabulary change.
acceptance_criteria: The rule names when a case table applies (one function, one setup) and when it does not (event order, sequences, code-text checks).
sprints.dev_notes: A rule goes in one place; the refactor skill points at it, never restates it. Decision 1 in the plan.

sprints.label: first-measurement
sprints.goal: Answer whether the planted bug data is good enough to drive the trimming. tests-that-catch-nothing and the trimming passes depend on the answer.
sprints.scope: Investigate: planted bugs (total, invalid, and the share of each outcome in section 3.3); assertions per piece (catches nothing, repeats others, unique); flaky assertions and repeated assertion identities; elapsed time. Findings go in docs/sprint-logs/test-dedup-first-measurement.md with a **Result:** line of Confirmed or Amend.
sprints.out_of_scope: Any change to code or tests.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict on the data: if crashes and timeouts credit no assertion for most caught planted bugs, the "repeats others" list is too thin to act on, and the plan needs a revision.
sprints.dev_notes: The run takes hours (an estimate); start it in the background. A negative verdict leads to a new plan revision, not an edit to this one.

sprints.label: refactor-skill-test-gate
sprints.goal: A refactor pass over a test piece keeps every planted bug caught.
sprints.scope: .agent/skills/refactor/SKILL.md. Main agent: when the input holds a test piece, it runs `measure` on the run's start commit in the background at step 1, and `sort` before the first find subagent for a test piece. Find subagent: for a test piece, it reads that piece's three lists; an assertion that repeats others is a Group A finding to drop; exception (decision 3): when its name, comment, or test group heading points to a past bug or issue, it stays, unless a kept assertion checks the exact same input, then it is a Group A drop too; merging tests into a case table is Group A only when AGENTS.md holds the case table rule; an assertion that catches nothing is a defect on main. Action subagent: after each cleanup to a test piece, it runs `prove` and reverts the cleanup on a failure. Review subagent: it runs `prove` on the branch and reports a failure as a defect in the branch's own changes.
sprints.out_of_scope: Running a pass; any test piece.
acceptance_criteria: Every step names the mode it runs and what a failure leads to.
No rule from AGENTS.md is restated; the skill points at it.
sprints.dev_notes: The measurement takes hours (an estimate), so the main agent starts it before the first file and waits on it only when the first test piece comes up.

sprints.label: tests-that-catch-nothing
sprints.goal: Each assertion on the spike's "catches nothing" list fails when its rule breaks, or goes to the product manager.
sprints.scope: The test pieces on the list. For each assertion: when it checks a rule of the product code, change its input so the rule matters, and confirm by breaking the rule by hand that it now fails, as #824 did; when it checks code text, docs, or the manifest, leave it; otherwise list it in the pull request for the product manager, with what it checks.
sprints.out_of_scope: Assertions that repeat others; any product code.
acceptance_criteria: Each repaired assertion fails with its rule broken and passes on the branch; the pull request states how each was broken.
`prove` against the spike's result file passes.
sprints.dev_notes: Assumes 10 to 30 assertions (an estimate); above 60, split by test piece into several pull requests. A repaired assertion changes the catch lists; that is the intent, and `prove` still passes because it checks for losses only.
